title: Shell Config Nuke
body:
In the installation part of the README.md, the use of the redirect operator `>` will cause the entire files contents to be overwritten. It should be changed to the append operator `>>`. If someone were to copy and paste it without version controlled dot files, it could lead to a very sad programmer.

`echo "alias lg='lazygit' > ~/.zshrc`
to
`echo "alias lg='lazygit'" >> ~/.zshrc`

title: Feature request: easy way to merge remote branch
body:
Congrats on lazygit, its great.

One of the slowest workflows with git is that to merge develop/master etc into your current branch  you have to stash/commit current, checkout master, pull, switch back to current, then merge. This is awfully slow in SourceTree.

There are two quicker ways on the command line, discussed in the stackoverflow answers here:

https://stackoverflow.com/a/34344502/2102158
`git pull origin master` - this effectively merges the origin version of develop into your branch in one command

https://stackoverflow.com/a/45697574/2102158
```
git fetch origin master:master
git merge master
```
Which updates the local master to the remote without a checkout, then merges it

In lazygit, I reckon the best would be to have a one key command to update a non checkout branch to latest - eg run `git fetch origin master:master` on it

Thanks for consideration.

title: Centos Packages
body:
This isn't an issue but more of an FYI.

I'm so impressed with this tool that I've created RPMs for Centos6 and Centos7 available on my public Yum repo: https://yum.jc21.com

For anyone interested, the RPM Spec file used is:

```
%global gh_commit   bc479a9bf5bee60cd3916b2c6d033ff266dfbd4d
%global gh_short    %(c=%{gh_commit}; echo ${c:0:7})

Name:           lazygit
Version:        0.1.25
Release:        1%{?dist}
Summary:        A simple terminal UI for git commands, written in Go with the gocui library.

Group:          Applications/System
License:        MIT
URL:            https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit
Source0:        https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/archive/v%{version}.tar.gz

BuildRequires:  git golang

%description
Are YOU tired of typing every git command directly into the terminal, but you're too stubborn to use Sourcetree because you'll never forgive Atlassian for making Jira? This is the app for you!

%prep
mkdir -p %{_builddir}/src/github.com/lazygit/
cd %{_builddir}/src/github.com/lazygit/
tar -xvzf %{_sourcedir}/v%{version}.tar.gz
mv lazygit-%{version} lazygit
cd lazygit

%build
export GOPATH="%{_builddir}"
export PATH=$PATH:"%{_builddir}"/bin
go get -u github.com/golang/dep/cmd/dep
cd %{_builddir}/src/github.com/lazygit/lazygit
dep ensure
go build -i -v -ldflags "-X main.Rev=%{gh_short} -X main.builddate=`date -u +%Y%m%d.%H%M%S`"
go install

%install
mkdir -p %{buildroot}%{_bindir}

cp %{_builddir}/bin/lazygit %{buildroot}%{_bindir}


%files
%{_bindir}/lazygit

%changelog
* Thu Aug 9 2018 Jamie Curnow <jc@jc21.com> 0.1.25-1
- v0.1.25 with commit hash

* Wed Aug 8 2018 Jamie Curnow <jc@jc21.com> 0.1.11-1
- Initial Spec File
```

Source RPMs are also available on the Yum site. Although I haven't tested, I'm pretty sure this spec file could be used to compile for Fedora too.

title: Installation via go get doesn't work due to unversioned binary
body:
According to README.md, lazygit can be installed via `go get`.
But lazygit executable binary that is installed via `go get` doesn't include version information. Then lazygit tries to read VERSION file in current directly, if there's not, lazygit goes panic as follows.

```bash
2018/08/09 12:00:59 open VERSION: no such file or directory
panic: open VERSION: no such file or directory


goroutine 1 [running]:
log.Panicln(0xc00009dec8, 0x1, 0x1)
	/home/pankona/work/go/src/log/log.go:340 +0xc0
main.fallbackVersion(0xc00009df48, 0x1)
	/home/pankona/go/src/github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/main.go:79 +0x11b
main.main()
	/home/pankona/go/src/github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/main.go:89 +0x2f0
```

lazygit downloaded from binary realeaes doesn't occur this problem. According to comments on `main.go`, Version information is embeded at compling time. I guess binary releases are compiled in appropriate way.

In my opinion, possible solutions for this situation are:
* Update README.md to introduce as "Do not to install via go get"
* Update README.md (and some files) to introduce how to build with embeded version information 
  * I think providing some automation (Makefile or something like easy shell scripting, etc) is better

If you have favorite idea among them (or you have another idea), let me know.
I may send a pull request for you. Thanks!

title: branches list showing phantom branches on case-insensitive file system
body: v0.1.48 The branches pane should really be using the output from `branch -a` and not `git reflog -n100 --pretty='%cr|%gs' --grep-reflog='checkout: moving' HEAD` as used in https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/9537645d0cfdac87addd4c9a5eb0e7df3bac8ee8/gitcommands.go#L577 for the list of what branches to show. Currently you will pick up all kinds of things that aren't real branches if you're on a case insensitive file system (default setting for macOS HFS+ volumes). ``` $ git init test $ cd test $ touch foo $ git add foo $ git commit -m "init" [master (root-commit) 00a9331] init 1 file changed, 0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-) create mode 100644 foo $ git branch -a * master $ git branch test $ git branch TEST fatal: A branch named 'TEST' already exists. $ git checkout TEST Switched to branch 'TEST' $ git checkout TeST Switched to branch 'TeST' $ git checkout TesT Switched to branch 'TesT' $ git checkout TEsT Switched to branch 'TEsT' $ git branch -a master test ``` meanwhile... ``` $ git reflog -n100 --pretty='%cr|%gs' 22 minutes ago|checkout: moving from TesT to TEsT 22 minutes ago|checkout: moving from TeST to TesT 22 minutes ago|checkout: moving from TEST to TeST 22 minutes ago|checkout: moving from master to TEST 22 minutes ago|commit (initial): init ```

title: File list re-ordered when staging files with spaces
body:
This is not a bug per-se, but a consequence of the behavior of `git status --untracked-files=all --short`. Observe:

```
$ git status --untracked-files=all --short
A  "asdf asdf"
A  lazygit
$ git reset HEAD asdf\ asdf 
$ git status --untracked-files=all --short
A  lazygit
?? asdf asdf
```
As you can see in the [source code](https://github.com/git/git/blob/master/wt-status.c#L1731), git will sometimes quote the path causing it to be re-ordered. While this is not a bug in lazygit, perhaps there should be a workaround to avoid surprising/bugging users.

title: Add a shortcut to open user editor to rename commit
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As of now, I don't think there's a way to rename the last commit in the user editor, while it's possible to do so when creating a new commit.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Ideally I'd like a shortcut to open the user editor to rename a commit.  <kbd> shift </kbd> + <kbd> R </kbd> seems intuitive since <kbd> shift </kbd> + <kbd> C </kbd> opens the user editor for a new commit. I know `lazygit` already uses <kbd> shift </kbd> + <kbd> R </kbd> for refreshing, but I don't think the two conflict with each other since they're meant to be used in different views, but I'm not totally sure.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I can always rename the commit in lazygit directly, but given that lazygit allows to enter a new commit in the user editor I think it'd be coherent to have the same feature for renaming.

**Additional context**
I'm happy to work on this and open a PR in the next few days if you think the feature is useful.
P.S. I'm loving this project! Keep up the good work!

title: FR: Better handling of deleting branches
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently we support deleting a branch with 'd' and force deleting a branch with 'D'. The latter has a confirmation panel to confirm you want to delete the branch.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We should just have a single 'd' keybinding and if git comes back telling us to use '-D' then we just swallow that error and show a confirmation prompt asking if they want to force delete.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
What we have now works but it's not ideal

title: FR: context menus for panels
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The options panel at the bottom of the screen which tells you which keybindings are available for the given panel should actually be accessible via a 'context menu' for a panel.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
On any panel, when you press '?' (or something like that) you should see a popup panel with a list of available options (prefixed by their keybindings in case you want to learn the keybindings). When you hit space on an option, it's interpreted as if you have pressed the corresponding keybinding.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Just showing a static popup panel with the keybindings

**Additional context**
This will help users who don't want to memorise keybindings, and fixes the issue of keybinding realestate at the bottom of the screen

title: FR: Custom commands
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It would be cool if we had an option for users to add their own custom commands via their config. We can define which variables will be available and then the command can refer to them via handlebars e.g.
`git reset --hard origin/{{branch}}`

Maybe for V1 we can just have them in an array and you access them via the 0-9 number keys. Later down the line we can have configurable keybindings where you can just define the keybinding as a custom command keybinding.

title: Support for non-printable symbols in diff view
body: It's really hard to determine what changes was made in some lines when some do trailing spaces clean-up or unifying tab policies when tabs converted to spaces or vice versa. So it would be nice to see actual difference for such changes and probably allow user to change visibility.

title: Asynchronous rendering of the Diff panel doesn't work
body:
**Describe the bug**
if you quickly flick through the panels, you'll often end up on the files panel but with a branch's log graph appearing in the diff panel. This is because we're now asynchronously rendering these things, and because the branch graph takes longer to obtain from git, it's the last to render to the diff view.

Seems to be only an issue with repos that have more commits in them.

Not sure what the standard approach to fixing this issue is, but we need some way to discard any writes to the diff panel that have been superceded by newer stuff.

flick through the panels and observe the log graph appears when the files panel is focused

the file's diff is shown

title: Enable easier switching between branches
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
So often I'll have some changes that I've made, and I realise I was supposed to make them on another branch, so I go to checkout that branch, then git tells me I need to stash my changes, so I stash my changes, checkout the other branch, then unstash, and now I'm where I want to be. But that's a lot of effort for a pretty simple process.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
In lazygit, if you try to checkout another branch and an error appears along the lines of 'must stash changes', there should be a confirmation panel that pops up and says 'would you like to use the stash to move your unstaged changes across?' and if you hit enter, it stashes your changes, checks out the branch, then unstashes your changes.

I think it should just leave the stashed changes there to be safe rather than delete it afterwards, but I'm happy to be convinced otherwise.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
a specific keybinding for checking out another branch in this way. I don't think that's necessary if we can get away with reading the error message and working out the situation, similar to how we don't have a keybinding for git push --force and instead show the confirmation panel because we infer from there being upstream commits that you might want to be force pushing.

**Additional context**
This sounds easy in my head to implement

title: Typing Custom Commands from within lazygit
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Leaving the terminal to run a custom command isn't the best user experience

**Describe the solution you'd like**
hitting 'X' to bring up a prompt where you can enter a command, and then the command runs as a subprocess (enabling you to enter input if required) and upon return a popup displays the output from the program (maybe we'll limit it to just stderr if there's a whole heap of output)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
1) just quitting lazygit and coming back
2) having everything happen from within a window in lazygit. This works well for commands like 'ls' which just return stuff, but it doesn't work for e.g. 'vim' which needs to have the whole screen. It would also be tricky to implement if we needed to support user input to the program
3) an approach where the user can specify what kind of program it is e.g. if it's vim we hit some other keystroke for 'full-screen command' or maybe we say what we want via a menu panel but that's an extra keystroke.
4) an approach where we run the program and if it's pumping out loads of characters, we switch to fullscreen mode. I'm not sure how feasible this is.

**Additional context**
With my WIP solution right now, it's a little jarring if we just run 'ls' to 1) see a flash because we switch to viewing the subprocess fullscreen and then come back, and 2) wait a while for the panels to load again because they're refetching data.

There is loads of room for improvement in terms of the speed at which those panels refresh after we come back from running a subprocess: things can be done parallel and we can take some logic out of the UI thread. But it's still gonna be a little jarring I think, and I don't like the idea of caching the data in case your command happened to be a git command that e.g. deleted a commit that lazygit now tries to inspect. Given the likelihood of entering in git commands this is going to happen a lot.

title: Discussion: Should we remove go modules support?
body:
At some point I made the decision to support go modules and I'm starting to regret it.

It may be that if we made the jump from go dep to go modules properly, rather than supporting both like we do now, it would fix the headache that we currently have.

But I've got no issue with go dep and it's workflow is really simple to follow, and to my knowledge removing go modules right now is a victimless crime. The only people affected would be those who pull down the source code and have go modules enabled in some strict way where they get an error if the project isn't using go modules.

I'm making this issue because I seem to continually bump into issues with go modules's checksum mismatches and just weird behaviour that I keep having to debug, and I can't see any point in it.

So please anybody who has an opinion let me know your thoughts :)

title: NOISSUE - Titles, labels and milestones
body:
As the title states this is not an issue, it is more or less a thread I want to start to talk about possible use of labels, titles and milestones. I had this idea, checking out projects like [mainflux](https://github.com/mainflux/mainflux) to use labels and titles to indicate what the issue or pull request is all about.

The issue titles would be:
 * NOISSUE - Title of an issue that is just for discussion.
 * BUG - Title of an issue that represents a bug.
 * FR - Title of an issue that represents a feature request.

The PR titles would be like: 
 * LG-123 - Title of a PR fixing issue 123.

If the PR is a WIP you can tag it as a "draft" using [this](https://github.blog/2019-02-14-introducing-draft-pull-requests/)

Labels would be like:
 * needs comment
 * gocui
 * git
 * config
 * core
 * urgent

The milestones would be representing releases like:
 * x.y.z

I hope to get lots of feedback on this! Let me know what you think!

title: Easy WIP commit creation
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
All the time I need to quickly change branches, and I want to store my current working directory changes against my branch as a WIP commit so that I can easily reset and keep going next time I check out the branch (the alternative of using the stash is not ideal because it's easy for things to get lost).

But rarely is my code in good enough shape to appease the linters in my pre-commit hooks.

using `git commit --no-verify` lets you bypass pre-commit hooks.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I want an easy way to create a WIP commit. I think the best solution is to have a hotkey dedicated to it, and when you hit that key, a commit message pops up saying 'WIP' and you can add more to it as you please. Then when you confirm, it does a commit with the --no-verify flag.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
adding the keybinding to the commit message panel itself rather than the files panel (where most keybindings go) to reduce clutter. This isn't ideal because there's no way to add the functionality for when you use shift+C and commit with your editor.

Skipping the text box and just directly committing with the message of 'WIP'. This is faster, but it means you can't enter in a meaningful message. I think if we express the fact that we're going to be skipping hooks in the title of the commit message panel, it'll be the same number of keypresses as if you had just shown a confirmation panel to confirm that the user wanted to commit their stuff without hooks.

**Additional context**
This would make my life much easier

title: Checking out commits
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We want to be able to checkout specific commits

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We need a keybinding for checking out commits. I would have liked to use space to mimic the behaviour in the branches panel but unfortunately we're using space for selecting commits to diff against.

Maybe we should give the space keybinding to this action, and find another keybinding for diffing commits. We can't use 'c' or shift+C because that's for copy+pasting commits. Maybe space is too easy to accidentally press and checking out a commit might be an unexpected action.

I'm open to suggestions :)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
none

**Additional context**
This is originally based on https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/issues/411

title: default config values aren't loaded properly
body:
**Describe the bug**
viper loads config values from yaml files as having lowercase keys, but we access them with mixed case. This means that if the user hasn't set their own config values manually in config.yml (where the values retain their mixed case) then the defaults will be ignored.

**To Reproduce**
without setting any config.yml file, hitting 'w' in the files panel should bring up the commit message panel with the skipHookPrefix value from the default config i.e. 'WIP'.

**Expected behavior**
defaults should be loaded, for example `git.skipHookPrefix: 'WIP'` (pending https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/pull/433 being merged)

What we actually get is an error message saying it's not configured.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: OSX
 - Lazygit adc74e

**Additional context**
There is a PR up for this which may be merged soon so the plan is to just bump the version once that PR is merged https://github.com/spf13/viper/pull/635

title: Using cobra as the argument parser.
body:
**Topic**
Right now we have an issue open #413 that requires us to parse a flag. We run/ran into troubles when we the arguments are formatted in a special way.

**Your thoughts**
We should use a library like [cobra](https://github.com/spf13/cobra) to make things easier for us to parse command line arguments. I think we should give it a try and see if it can make things easier for us.

**consequences**
We would have to rewrite the way lazygit starts up. And we might have to restructure the project a bit (see the cobra page) but after that we would be able to add commands and cli arguments to the project without any trouble.

Let me know what you guys think!

title: [FEATURE REQUEST] Shift + J/K as alternative to PageUp/Down (Scroll)
body:
**Problem**
Using PageUp and PageDown to scroll the righthand window is not intuitive.
It makes user's hands get out of keyboard's home row, which is inconvenient and (I think) anti pattern in vim-ish keybinding.

**Solution**
Even though you provide workaround at #423 , but I think setting <S-j> (Shift + j) for scroll up and <S-k> (Shift + k) for scroll down will be more intuitive, as it prevent user's hand get out of the keyboard's home row.

**Alternative**
Make both PageUp/Down and <S-k/j> available

title: Better handeling of "not a git repository"
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When someone types lazygit in a not git repo it craches

**Describe the solution you'd like**
First of all crashing isn't the right behaviour because nothing is broken, the user is just in a wrong dir without the `.git` folder.  

But what i personally would like to see is a popup with the recently visited git repos where i can select a repo to use in lazygit.  
Beside that it would be nice if it's possible change the current work dir from the opened repo.  

That way it's easy to go to a recently opened git repo from anywhere on the system and when someone would like to make changes to that repo they can just press something like `shift + Q` to quit and change there current working dir to lazygit's git repo dir.  

Often when i work on projects i have multiple terminal tabs open in multiple git repos but to get these tabs open after a system bootup it takes a stupid long time. When having the above in lazygit this can be solved because lazygit already knows all my visited repos the `cd ../../../someGitServer/user/project` can be replaced with opening lazygit, select a recently opened git repo and do a quit + change the current dir.  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- **CD into a project.**  
Yes most people will have no problem with that and i agree but when having to deal with for example multiple micro services over multiple git repo's from multiple origins this gets annoying very quickly 

- **Use a smarter shell like fish/zsh**  
From the things i have used to make chaining long dirs easier this is one of the best solutions for changing the dir fast, fish has a nice feather where it suggests the path for you and it works oke but it still often suggest the half path because because i'm to lazy to type the full path every time like: (where i meant to directly go further `~/go/src/github.com/mjarkk/somerepo`)![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15320763/

title: Ignore tracked files
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
If you want to ignore a file, but that file is tracked, git gives you an error. You can untrack these files with the following commands:
```
$ git rm -r --cached .
$ git add .
```

Based on https://www.git-tower.com/learn/git/faq/ignore-tracked-files-in-git

**Describe the solution you'd like**
If we try to ignore something that is tracked, we should do what git tower does and ask if we want to perform this cleanup under the hood

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None

**Additional context**
None

body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, if you have some files you want to keep working on, and some files you want to stash, you need to
1) make a commit with the changes you want to keep
2) stash the changes you do not want to keep
3) hard reset to HEAD~1

**Describe the solution you'd like**
When we press 'S' to stash, now we get a menu asking if we want to stash all changes, or stash staged changes.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An option to stash unstaged changes. But I don't think this would make as much sense. If you have staged changes you want to keep, then those actually would make sense being committed.

**Additional context**
this stack overflow page demonstrates that there is really no easy way to do this with the command line https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14759748/stashing-only-staged-changes-in-git-is-it-possible

title: Renaming file shrinks the Files list but the cursor doesn't follow
body:
**Topic**
Whenever files are renamed, they end up listed twice because of the Deleted ones and the Added ones. Once both the Deleted and Added version of the files are staged, it becomes a Rename, which means rather than having 2 lines, we get only 1. When doing so, the cursor stays at the same position in regard to the Files box, but both the Deleted file and the Added file get moved down to be Renamed. It causes the cursor to be 2 lines lower in regard to its position relative to the file names.

![lazygit-cursor](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1949339/61959864-52c15a00-af92-11e9-9f8b-7397144ab64e.gif)

**Your thoughts**
Since the number of items in the list changes and the filename under the cursor is merged with another one to become a Rename, we cannot really do much to prevent the list from moving. 

The only behavior that could make sens is if the cursor follows the list moving and end up being on the item below its original position. For instance, when I select the file `11` and below it there's `12` and then `13`, the cursor could end on `12` rather than `13`. It would mean moving the cursor up once.

Would this behavior make sens? Could we even detect that situation and add that behavior?

title: Manual resolution of merge conflict

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

First, I wanted to say thank you for making such an awesome tool. 
When I want to resolve a merge conflict, I have this issue where oftentimes, I need to modify directly the file that contains a conflict, since using both hunks will cause duplicated information. So in order to do this right now, I have to exit lazygit, open up my text editor, resolve the change manually, then open up lazygit and finish the merge.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.

It would be nice to add an option to make a file edit to resolve the merge. That way it could open up the preferred editor to that file to allow us to make the corresponding change to resolve the conflict and then have us land right back in lazygit to stage the change and finish the merge.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.

I'm not quite sure if there's any better way but to either open up an external editor or to allow edits inline, but I'm not sure if that is necessary given that it's a very specific use case to build in full text editing functionality.

title: Unable to Update when Compiled from Go
body:
**Describe the bug**
At any time, when `lazygit` is compiled via `go build` checking for a new version (`u`) fails as;

    Update failed: rename /tmp/lazygit{string}/lazygit /home/username/.go/bin/lazygit: invalid cross-device link

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Run `lazygit` in any git repository
2. Highlight `Status` and press `u` to check for updates
3. Hit `enter` to accept update
4. View heinous error

**Expected behavior**
Expected to replace the binary (which it can clearly find) with the new version.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Arch
 - Lazygit Version: commit 827837b0b940d9367cefd03eb0e779711f9489da
 - The last commit id: 827837b0b940d9367cefd03eb0e779711f9489da

**Additional context**
Updates if you compiled via Go, are broken. :( Additionally, if you compiled with `go build` there is no version number. It simply says `unversioned` which is a real bummer.

On a hunch, I tried with `sudo`. Same errors. 

`/tmp/lazygit........` also does not exist like you would expect it to.

IIRC, `invalid cross-device link` usually happens when hard-links are across storage devices. My entire root file system is on a single partition.

I'd consider this option only for the _C_ key (commit with editor), not for the _c_ key.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
To have a configuration option to pass whatever desired options to the different git commands.
Something like `git.commit.options` where I'd have to assign `--signoff` to get that option active.

**Additional context**
My current console GUI is _tig_, where I've configured `~/.tigrc` with `bind status C !git commit --signoff` for this matter.

title: show related commits when a file is selected
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It would be cool if when you've selected a file, the commits panel highlights commits that include that file in their changes.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We could next to the commit sha a little status string like 'M' for modified, 'A' for added etc, for the selected file. This would make it easier to know which commit to amend/fixup when you're making a change to a file but don't want it to be in a new commit.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
filtering the list of commits as well, but this could cause some confusion unless we made it only happen when you hit a certain key

**Additional context**
We might need to asynchronously store all the files inside commits inside the commit struct so that it's not too expensive to do this. And we might need to store the selected filename separately so that we can still scroll through the commits

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Usually when i'm working on a big change for a large project i write a shitload of code and when i'm dune i commit the changes i think are most important.  

If there are only 20 files changed this can be easily dune using lazygit but when i have more than 100 or more files changed and only 80 of then need to be committed this gets a bit frustrating because the current files panel is quite small and it's frustrating to press 100 times down to get to un-stash 1 file

A shortcuts for chaining the files panel to a bigger and easier file selector that also includes folders.  
I imagine it could look something like this:  
```
src/
  controllers/
    users/
      users.go
      edit.go
  helpers/
    database/
      db.go

A user can navigate using the arrow keys, for example when the user is inside controllers and presses down helpers will be selected. If the user presses right from controllers users will be selected. If pressed space on a folder the full folder will be stashed.  
*just supper lazy :)*

I normally just use the terminal if there are so many files to stash but this is also frustrating if there are many nested folders

title: The "reset selection" function in the "Unstaged Changes" section should be removed
body:
... until there's either undo functionality in the system or something else

**Topic**
The "reset selection" (<kbd>d</kbd>) key on the "Unstaged Changes" panel.

title: Feature Request: Allow environment variable based config selection
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'd like to set up lazygit to follow the changes to my terminal theme based on my mac's light/dark mode. My iterm2 client is configured to do this, I'd like to define an environment variable that stores the status of light/dark theme and use that to determine which config to load when opening lazygit. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The ability to have sections of the config load conditionally based on an environment variable. e.g. have a light-theme: true section with colors and a light-theme: false section with its own colors and only load the applicable config section based on `LAZYGIT_THEME` or something.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
When loading lazygit, it searches for an environment variable such as `LAZYGIT_SELECTED_CONFIG` and will load the config with that name. This would also require the ability to save/edit multiple configs.

title: Use libgit2/git2go instead of command line git
body:
**Topic**
There's a library called [`lib2git`](https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2) that has a library made to integrate with `git` without having to run command line options in sub shell like (I believe) y'all are currently doing.

Said project has `go` bindings as well at [`git2go`](https://github.com/libgit2/git2go).

**Your thoughts**
This is mostly just an "FYI, this thing exists which might be better/useful". title: Pull/push doesn't find remote specified in [branch] config
body:
**Describe the bug**
I use [hub](https://github.com/github/hub) to checkout PRs for review. By issuing `hub checkout <url>` it will checkout from a fork without adding the fork as a remote. This can be handy when managing local mess when checking contributions from tens/hundreds of different contributors.

lazygit doesn't seem to recognise these [branch] configuration entries, prompting for a remote URL when hitting `p` to pull. It would be great if it could understand they are there!

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use `hub` to checkout a pull request, or alternative manually add a branch configuration to `.git/confg` for a project:

```
[branch "dropdown_keyboard_support"]
        remote = https://github.com/UselessToucan/osu-framework.git
        merge = refs/heads/dropdown_keyboard_support
```
2. Checkout branch
3. Try to pull within lazygit
4. See prompt for remote URL, even though it should already be known

**Expected behavior**
Expect the pull to run without prompting. This is also applicable to push operations, for what it's worth.

**Screenshots**

title: Ability to reset active branch to tracking
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

One scenario I encounter semi-regularly is completely destroying a local branch tracking `master` or otherwise (ie. merging multiple PRs to do some ad-hoc integration testing) and once done, resetting my local branch to its upstream tracking branch.

On CLI I would do this by issuing something along the lines of `git reset --hard upstream/master`, but this doesn't seem possible currently.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Either an explicit command in the `Local Branches` area to reset to tracking branch, or the ability to use the "reset" command (usually only available in the `Commits - Reflog`) in the `Remotes` area, just allowing resetting to `HEAD` on any remote.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

In some cases if you haven't mangled the branch too much, you can already achieve roughly this behaviour by resetting back to an old commit in the commits view, then fast-forwarding back to sane state.

title: More ways to reset the current branch
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We need more ways to reset the current branch to something else. Currently in the files panel, shift+D lets you soft/hard reset to HEAD, as well as hard reset to @{upstream}. You can also soft/hard/mixed reset onto a selected commit by pressing 'g'

It would be good to be able to bring up a menu when any local or remote branch is selected and be able to soft/hard/mixed reset onto the HEAD of that branch.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
given we're not using the 'g' keybinding elsewhere (that I can tell), we should use that for resetting the current branch to the selected item, be it commit, or local/remote branch. resetting to HEAD is a kind of worktree deleting action so I don't have an issue keeping it under the shift+D keybinding, and you'll be able to do it in the local branch panel anyway by selecting the current branch, so I'll keep that as it is. 

I think that pressing 'g' on the files panel should bring up the reset options for the upstream branch. This is the only one that would break the pattern: in that the selected item (a file in this case) is irrelevant to the command. But that doesn't bother me too much

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
none

**Additional context**
we currently have the `git reset --hard @{upstream}` command in the files panel under shift+D, but I only really put it there for myself and I'm happy to remove it once the better solution is made.

title: Check if index.lock exists and warn / act appropriately
body:
It just has happened to me that if, for whatever reason, a git repo I want to work with using lazygit is locked by another process (or some former process crashed), lazygit does nothing anymore. This is due to a (left over) `index.lock` file in the repo's .git local directory.

In this case, when lazygit is trying to stage files, it consumes a lot of CPU time and/or hangs completely. Tested with 0.14.3. 

Using the regular git CLI (`git`) spits out the warning
`fatal: Unable to create '.git/index.lock': File exists`

Manually removing the (stale) index.lock file or quitting the concurring program makes lazygit work again.

lazygit should check and warn if it can't do anything sensible in that case and/or bail out more gracefully if possible.

title: Idea for browsing a submodule

I think I've got an idea while writing this request (wrote my first idea but found a better one and erased most of the message)

So, as far as I can see lazygit is able to understand that folder is a submodule. In this case "b" key could be used for "Browse Submodule" command. In that call lazygit can trigger another lazygit in submodules folder with a command line parameter "--parent_repo=<parent_repo_path>".

If that parameter exists, lazygit also can return to that parent repo via opening another lazygit instance int parent repo path on program exit.

One thing could be an issue: Can a console program close itself and then run another console program at the same time?

title: Predefined commit messages
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It would be good to have an option to set predefined commit messages per repository. For example, at work, we use Jira, and we prefix all the commits with ticket number, and also all branch names contains the ticket number, for example:
* Branch name - feature/AB-123
* Commit name - [AB-123] Adding a feature.
Sometime it happens that i mistype the ticket number in the commit. It can be fixed of course, but why not fix the cause if possible :)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I assume this could be part of the global configuration, or maybe to introduce project local configuration (.lazygitrc maybe?) If there's better idea, let me know.
For example, configuration could have something like a defined parser that would know how to extract `AB-123` and set it as default value for commit message when opened. This is a bit tricky because parsing needs to be done using some language.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Since i'm a vim user, I set up an VimEnter autocommand that checks if i'm editing a commit message, and then parse the value from the branch and append it. It works fairly well, but i mostly use lazygit commit messages.
Here's link to vim code if you are interested: https://github.com/kristijanhusak/neovim-config/blob/master/nvim/partials/filetype/gitcommit.vim

This is maybe too big of a hassle for such a small feature, but i'm open for suggestions.

title: Provide an option to pass `--work-tree` to git
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I have a repo that I use to store my dotfiles, which is essentially a bare repo that I can use from anywhere just passing some arguments: `git --git-dir=$HOME/dotfiles/ --work-tree=$HOME`. `--git-dir` in this case is pointing to the bare repo (in this case, I think I could use the flag `--path` provided by lazygit), and `--work-tree` is pointing to my home folder, which is the root where I store the dotfiles (for more info, it is basically what is described in https://www.atlassian.com/git/tutorials/dotfiles).

So, TL;DR; Apparently, lazygit provides no way of configuring the --work-tree, so I can't use it on this repo.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be nice to have either a specific config for this, like `--work-tree=$HOME` (same as was done on https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/pull/414 with `--git-dir`), which would default to the git dir if you don't pass.
Another solution would be to have a config with a list of arguments to pass to git anytime lazygit calls it, like `--git-args="--work-tree=$HOME"`, and then lazygit would execute `git --work-tree=$HOME"`, instead of just `git`, which would make lazygit a lot more flexible.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None that I can think of, other than using just git directly

**Additional context**
N/A


What do you think?

**UPDATE 2025**
Starting from upcoming lazygit 0.55, you will be able to opt in for git's existing external diff setup by configuring:

```yaml
git:
  paging:
    # If true, Lazygit will use git's `diff.external` config for paging. The advantage over `externalDiffCommand` is that this can be configured per file type in .gitattributes; see https://git-scm.com/docs/gitattributes#_defining_an_external_diff_driver.

```

Trace/BPT trap: 5

```

It appears this is because [Go 1.13 only supports macOS version 10.10+](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/35269#issuecomment-548677490).

It would be good if the ReadMe/Release Notes specified the minimum Mac OS version as 10.10 (or whatever the current minimum Go-supported OS version is).

Also, I think this means that there's no point in have a 32-bit build available as I think the last 32-bit only Mac OS X was [10.7/Snow Leopard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_OS_X_Snow_Leopard)?

[user]

title: Ability to use existing shell for commands and git actions
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
If you have a git hook before push/commit and it depends on a certain tool e.g. node then it is best to use the current shell.

For example I have `nvm` and various node versions. In the git hook it runs tests using node and it expects a certain version. I load the correct version by `nvm use v8` but lazygit still complains about wrong version and stops all the commits and pushes. That is because I image it is running in a separate shell like when you run custom commands, and in that shell `nvm` never switched to required version.

This is the same issue when you run custom commands, it runs `bash -c ...`. Firstly now you need to format your commands for bash instead of default shell/current shell which is very annoying (especially for `fish` users where syntax is different). And you cannot use local variables, and some time even all commands as you might not have updated `.bashrc` to include all paths that are there in your current/default shell; since you never use it.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Run all custom commands and git commands in current shell process.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternative is using `git` directly from current shell and not using `lazygit`.

title: Some sort of sandbox mode
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Often I'm to lazy to learn new git features in a separate repo and i'm to scared to use them in a production repo so in the end i usually just stick to the things i already know.  
But there are just times when you just need to use them and usually that means i just make a copy of the folder i'm working in and start messing around in that folder.    
Lazygit makes these features a lot more accessible and a lot less scary but I'm often still to scared to try them out when I'm messing around in a branch that has for example 1 month of work inside of it.  
I know that most git features are reversible but that's not where my brain is once i realize i just "removed" a month of work with a git command i understand for 50%.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Something like: `lazygit try`
1. It copies the current working dir to `../.{working-dir-name}-lazygit-try` (might be worth showing a short message what this command does and ask if they want to continue)
2. Opens the preferred shell in that folder
3. When lazygit is opened inside this shell it can detect it is in "Try" state and adds some extra functionality like:
    - reset everything (panic button)
    - commit the changes made in the try dir to the original dir and quit
    - disable git features like pushing
4. When the shell is quit the lazygit that spawned the shell can ask the user for what they want like:
    - if want to destroy all changes
    - keep the changes made in the try dir
    - show the executed git commands

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Learning git features in a repo meant for that or just manually copying a production repo to another folder and tryout things in there.   

**Additional context**
It's really just an ultra safe way of experimenting with git features in production repos without the fear of breaking things and with tools to keep the bar low like with one push of a button all

title: support rebasing from a specific commit
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I want to be able to rebase from a specific commit onto another branch i.e. `git rebase --onto baseBranch COMMIT_SHA`. This is good for when your rebase has changed a lot and you don't want to replay the base branch's original commits back on top of the new ones (this often causes conflicts).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We need a way to both select the base branch as well as the base commit on the current branch. I'm thinking the rebase confirmation when you press 'r' on a branch becomes a rebase menu where one option is to specify the base commit. After selecting that, focus would be given to the local commits context to select the base commit. Then when you select it the rebase begins.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could be stateful and actually mark the base commit ourselves before opening the rebase menu. That way it's implicit that that's the commit you want to rebase from. This would be easier to implement in terms of the UI and also would mean that subsequent rebases don't require you to re-select that commit. The complexity would be added in maintaining the state across lazygit runs in a file, and also handling things like rebase events that remove that commit SHA (we could simply remove the base commit marker in those situations and leave it up to the user to re-set it). I'm actually thinking this approach makes more sense now.

**Additional context**
Just found myself needing this today

title: Handle repos that use 'main' as the main branch
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

GitHub and git are now using 'main' instead of 'master' for the default branch name.  lazygit only considers 'master', and colors 'main' as a branch instead of the default branch.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

git can now be configured to use any name as the default branch with the following config snippet:

```
[init]
        defaultBranch = main
```

lazygit should ~~use the defaultBranch option for~~ programatically determine the branch to color as master, and fall back to 'master' or 'main' if it's not present.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

title: Better default local branch name when checking out from remote
body:
I was in a repository and wanted to check out a branch, but didn't know the name.  I had never checked out that branch before.  So I thought to browse the existing remote branches to see if I could find the right one from the commit graph.

Bingo!  Lazygit made that really easy!  I started it, I hit `3` to go to the Branches pane, then I hit `]` to go to the Remotes tab in that pane.  Then I was able to hit Enter on the remote "origin" and that showed me all branches, and selecting one showed me the commits.

The branch "feature/foo" was what I wanted.  So I hit Space on it, expecting to get a local branch named "feature/foo" tracking this remote branch.  But lazygit is more flexible than this: it pops up a dialog where I can enter the name of the local branch.  Very nice.

But the default name it proposes is "origin/feature/foo", and I believe I nearly never want that "origin/" prefix.

I suggest to default to "feature/foo", instead.

But it's possible I have misunderstood lazygit, and I went about this in the wrong way.  What I did was just poke around in a blond way and lazygit kind of lead me to this place.  If I was too blond, I apologize :-)

title: enhancements for repos using hooks
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We use hooks on our repos, most especially at push-time, but because we're using `pre-git` (it makes life easier), even a commit without pre-commit logic can take a second or two, during which time I'm not sure if I've hit `enter` or not on the commit dialog

**Describe the solution you'd like**
short-term: the same kind of feedback that's on the Push dialog would be nice on the commit dialog (ie label and spinner)

longer-term: our push hooks can take a while. One runs the full test suite (takes around 80s) and many run a `verify-up-to-date` task which won't let you push a satellite branch if you're behind master. Both produce output, which lazygit will display if they fail (I've seen the `verify-up-to-date` output on occasion), but I'd really like a live output of commands as they are running, configured, of course, to user prefs (so the feedback dialog should be default and the details could be shown if, eg, `gui.showDetailedOperations` were set). Details should be shown _live_ though -- there's not much point in seeing the output from a long operation way after it already successfully completed, but seeing it _during_ operation provides feedback to the user

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I wait after I _think_ I've hit enter on commit. Usually I have, but it's been a good test of holding my breath.

The last time I pushed on the project which runs tests, I exited lazygit so I could watch the tests roll by.

title: Minor wording inconsistency: Confirmation prompts

title: Picking hunks does not work for files handled via git-lfs
body:
**Describe the bug**

I rebased a branch onto another branch.  A file `foo.zip` was modified in both branches.  So naturally there was a conflict on rebasing.  The "Files" portion of the UI (where the files are listed with A or M or something on the left) showed something unusual, but unfortunately I do not remember what exactly it was showing.  I know it had two letters on the left instead of only one, but I forgot which letters exactly.

I didn't know what exactly to do, so I hit x to show the menu.  I found the command to show rebase/merge options.  This gave me a popup to allow me to choose abort or continue -- not what I was looking for.  I wanted to decide what to do with this file.

Anyway, I was confused what to do, so I hit Enter on that line and this showed me two hunks and allowed me to pick one.  It also mentioned a "size" and I knew I wanted the larger `foo.zip`, so I selected that hunk with space.

At first, I was elated because the rebase succeeded.  Very slick, I thought.

The result was that `foo.zip` was replaced with a short text file, probably similar to the following:

```
version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1
oid sha256:32faba9a7dea5e89e597ff4d01fa97f307065cbbde48f110e012f12c9a8a14cf
size 1440546
```

I don't know for sure that this file was handled via git-lfs, but I am just guessing based on the words in the first line of the file.

I don't know what lazygit should do, but I feel that it shouldn't clobber files like this.  Maybe it could recognize that the file is handled by git-lfs and then avoid allowing the user to select a hunk?  Maybe some other kind of dialog that allows me to choose one of the two files?

title: Informational prompt?
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In our project we use git describe all the time for issue tracking. I implemented a custom command that sort of does what I want but I'm interested if you have ever thought about informational only prompts. I.e. not 'input' or 'menu', just outputting the result of something like git describe. There may be other use cases for informational prompts but lg is pretty comprehensive and I'm struggling to think of anything else where you haven't covered my bases already.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like to have a bound customCommand that pops up the prompt and exits perhaps on Esc or Enter (doesn't matter, whichever makes sense to you).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Here's what I implemented, which works fine but it feels a bit like a context switch:
```
customCommands:
  - key: 'D'
    command: 'git describe'
    context: 'commits'
    subprocess: true
```
I can also use the ':' option and type in git describe as an on-the-fly custom command from the localBranches or commits tabs. Also a workable solution but also feels context switchy. And I'd prefer a single command to typing the full command each time.

**Additional context**
Thanks so much for lg. A few of my colleagues and I love it.

title: Maintain cursor position in menu after exiting submodule
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
If you enter and exit a submodule from the Files menu, the file selection cursor jumps back to the top of the file list, forcing you to scroll back down to where the cursor was previously. This can be frustrating, especially if the repo has a large number of submodules, as lots of unnecessary scrolling will be necessary.

The cursor position is maintained when using the enter/exit keybindings on regular files in the Files menu (i. e. to enter and exit staging specific hunks). I think this behavior should carry over to submodules as well, as it would make things much more consistent.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Remember the cursor position in the Files menu of the parent repo when entering a submodule and return to the same location after exiting the submodule.

Also, thank you for writing this tool -- it's by far the best git UI I've used.

title: Sensible Defaults
body:
It's not always clear what makes a sensible default, because different people will use lazygit differently. Furthermore, changing the default for something could be jarring to a user who is familiar with the old way of doing it. On the other hand, if a default brings enough value, it's worth making the change, especially when any aggrieved users can always configure lazygit to have the old behaviour.

One recent default change was to no longer quit lazygit upon pressing 'esc' at the top level. I think that was a pretty reasonable change and nobody complained. Some other changes I'm thinking of:

1) Defaulting to file tree view
2) Defaulting to showing the command log (https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/pull/1246)

I think that defaults should be done with newbies in mind, because it's not hard to change the default if you don't like it.

At any rate this issue is dedicated to all things related to sensible defaults

title: Reading env variable from configuration file or allowing "local" configuration override
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'm using lazygit on multiple machines. Most of the time I'm on desktop, where I use light theme, because I work on it during the day, but when I'm on a laptop, I'm usually in a dark room and I switch to dark theme. I have a script that toggles all this configuration for me, and that script currently also toggles my lazygit configuration like this:

```
'sed -i "s/lightTheme.*/lightTheme: ' + is_light + '/g" ~/.config/lazygit/config.yml'
```

Recently my lazygit configuration grew because I introduced some of the custom commands and everything, because of which I had to make my lazygit config private. I'm syncing it to Dropbox and symlinking it to the right place on every machine.
This introduces the problem if I used different color scheme on multiple machines. Once I switch it on one machine, Dropbox syncs it everywhere and breaks my configuration on other machine.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like to have 2 ways to approach this issue:

1. Allow reading env variables from configuration. That way I could just set env variable on my machine, and read it in configuration file. Something like this:
```yml
gui:
  theme:
    lightTheme: $LAZYGIT_THEME
```
2. Having a way to extend the configuration with some "local" configuration. As far as I know yml doesn't allow any importing or extending, so I'm not sure how this could be achieved. First solution seems much simpler, but this one would also work, and is more flexible.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I don't have any ideally working alternative for this. I could just copy from Dropbox instead of symlinking it, but then I have to copy it on every machine on every change.

```shell

title: Suggestion: add ability to edit hunk
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Lazygit makes it really easy to select specific lines to be staged, however sometimes I need more flexibility.

For example, I have these unstaged changes:

```diff
 export const demo = Demo.Collection.fromComponent(UserStatsSubRoute)({
-  name: 'UserStats',
-  children: [StatsGraphDemo, MilestonesDemos],
+  name: displayName,
+  children: [StatsGraphDemo, UsesDemo, MilestonesDemos],
 });
```

I only want to add the change to `name`, not to `children`.

If I select the `name` line addition/deletion, I end up with this staged diff:

```diff
 export const demo = Demo.Collection.fromComponent(UserStatsSubRoute)({
-  name: 'UserStats',
   children: [StatsGraphDemo, MilestonesDemos],
+  name: displayName,
 });
```

What I wanted:

```diff
 export const demo = Demo.Collection.fromComponent(UserStatsSubRoute)({
-  name: 'UserStats',
+  name: displayName,
   children: [StatsGraphDemo, MilestonesDemos],
 });
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The ability to "edit hunk" similar to what is available when you run `git add --interactive` and use the `e` command.

This would make it easy for me to stage the changes because I would be able to delete and re-order the order of the addition/deletions.

Go to the files panel

I would expect to see a typically conflict diff in the merge conflicts panel.

title: When a conflict occurs during rebase, show which commit was being applied
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When I rebase and there's a conflict, I like to look at the original commit (pre-rebase) to help me remember what the commit was doing so I can handle the conflict appropriately.

When I perform a rebase using the git CLI, when a conflict occurs, git logs the commit it was trying to apply when the conflict occurred:

```sh-session
$ git rebase --interactive master
CONFLICT (modify/delete): app/services/api/photos/types.ts deleted in HEAD and modified in 218c9455f2... Move types into photo modules. Version 218c9455f2... Move types into photo modules of app/services/api/photos/types.ts left in tree.
error: could not apply 218c9455f2... Move types into photo modules
Resolve all conflicts manually, mark them as resolved with
"git add/rm <conflicted_files>", then run "git rebase --continue".
You can instead skip this commit: run "git rebase --skip".
To abort and get back to the state before "git rebase", run "git rebase --abort".
Could not apply 218c9455f2... Move types into photo modules
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
When I perform a rebase using lazygit, when a conflict occurs, lazygit should show the commit which was being applied when the conflict occurred—similar to how the git CLI works. For example, it could show this in the command log.

title: Keep track of commands history across the sessions
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Recently you introduced command history, which is really great. It would save my ass if I would check it immediately. Unfortunately I left lazygit and the history was gone. I changed so many files that I lost a track of what I discarded. Having at least the file name that I discarded would help a lot.
My idea is just to keep the history in some cache file, for at least some amount of time. Something like bash does with `.bash_history` or zsh with `.zsh_history`. Of course, this would be an opt-in feature.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
For now I'll add a `confirmOnQuit` to slow me down a little bit, but I don't know anything else that I could do. Maybe unbind `d` and have discard on something else where I need to think before doing it.

**Additional context**
I believe this shouldn't be too hard to implement, since data is there. It just needs to be appended to the cache file when lazygit is closed.

When I'm using gitflow and I need the create a feature while having uncommited/unstashed changes, I'm not allowed. When I hit `i`, and try to create a feature I have to cancel, then stash my changes, create the feature and finally pop the stash.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
When I create a feature by using the `i` shortcut, it would be useful to automatically:
- Stash changes using the same name as the branch to be created.
- Create/checkout said branch
- Pop stash

This will allow me to simply hit `i` and create my feature without worrying about unstashed changes.

body:
**Describe the bug**
My character set, ISO-8859-15 (Latin9), is not supported.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
```
$ git init test
Initialized empty Git repository in /tmp/test/.git/
$ lazygit
2021/05/26 15:22:01 An error occurred! Please create an issue at: https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/issues

$ echo $?
1
$ echo $LC_CTYPE
en_US.ISO-8859-15
$ echo $LANG
en_US.ISO-8859-15
$
```

**Expected behavior**
lazygit should work without problems.

From what I see on the screenshots/casts, all characters could be replaced by even 7-bit ASCII variants:
- up/down arrow in status panel: ^/v or u/d

**Desktop:**

**References**
Might be related to #24 and #422.

title: Compilation on Raspberry Pi 4 failes (see solution provided)
body:
Could not compile lazygit on a Raspberry Pi 4. 

Solution to this issue was to run: 
```
go get -u golang.org/x/term
env GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm GOARM=6 go build
```
This then successfully ran the compilation and lazygit can be run on the Raspberry Pi 4. 

I don't know much about Go but it seems that this x/term package seems to be missing on the Pi 4 by default?

title: Crash on setting upstream with "ambigous" name.
body:
**Describe the bug**

This is somewhat related to https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/issues/884 and https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/issues/833. Lazygit crashes if one uses the "default" workflow of not renaming the remote branch when creating a local one from it, and then trying to set the upstream branch

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

- Go to Branches Panel
- Press `]` to navigate to remotes. Press `Enter` on line with remote branch count to populate remote branches list.
- Scroll to the remote branch you want to checkout locally and press `n` and then enter. 
- Press `]`, `Enter` again, and scrol to the same remote branch as above. Press `u` and `Enter`. Observe the crash in the `Sceenshots` section below.

**Expected behavior**

At the very minimum not to crash. However, it seems that it does not make sense to have local branch that includes the "origin/" prefix of the remote branch. Everyone is deleting this "origin/" anyway.  So why not let Lazygit strip it off in the first place? It (probably) never makes sense to leave it in anyway.

As a side note, in the line editor `Home` and `End` button do not seem to work so you have to press left arrow a zillion times to get to the line beginning in order to remove the "origin/" prefix. Can we support `Home` and `End` please?

title: Switch between multiple log views
body:
I use the log graph in a couple of different ways. One is to quickly see all the commits, in which case I use `oneline` with a cutoff so that many commits are displayed in the log graph in `1 -> a`. Sometimes, I need to switch back and forth between `oneline` and the default (since the default gives me a lot more default of a particular commit).

Currently, I have set the `allBranchesLogCmd` to be a particular command (e.g. oneline logs with a cutoff). But sometimes I would like to see the expanded log with full commit description, branches, files etc (i.e. the default version of `1 -> a`).

title: Recursive submodule checkout
body:
If I'd like to check out an older commit, lazygit only checks out that commit in the main repo, not the related submodules. This creates also a problem if the user clones a repo for the first time. I usually get a false idea that I haven't done something wrong (because submodules are marked as modified) but it is because they are not in sync with the current commit.

It would be good if we could have checked out those submodules recursively. Of course, they could be dirty, then an error message could be shown to the user about it.

title: Error when cherry-picking a merge commit
body:
**Describe the bug**
Cherry-picking a merge commit results in error `Rebasing (1/1)error: commit ... is a merge but no -m option was given.`

**To Reproduce**

Try cherry-picking any merge commit, or use this script to create a test git repo with a merge commit that is ready to be cherry-picked:
```
@echo off

git init

echo v1 > a.txt
git add a.txt
git commit -m v1

:: We will cherry-pick our merge commit to branch "release".
git branch release

:: Add the "work" branch with a couple of commits.
git checkout -b work
echo v2 > a.txt
git add a.txt
git commit -m work2
echo v3 > a.txt
git add a.txt
git commit -m work3

:: Merge "work" into "main". Use "--no-ff" to force creating a new merge commit.
git checkout main
git merge --no-ff work

:: Switch to the "release" branch.
git checkout release

echo Now, open lazygit and cherry-pick the merge commit from the "main" branch to "release" branch.
```

Actual behavior: lazygit shows an error message `Rebasing (1/1)error: commit ... is a merge but no -m option was given.`


**Expected behavior**
The merge commit is expected to be cherry-picked without any errors.

 - Lazygit Version v0.28.2

title: Support for quering refs in custom commands!
body:
First of all, thanks for building such a useful piece of software; been using lazygit for a while and I really like it!

## Is there a way to (dynamically) generate menu entries out of remote branches for example

I have this custom command in my config:
```
  - key : 'r'
    description: 'Checkout a remote ref as FETCH_HEAD'
    command: "git fetch {{index .PromptResponses 0}} {{index .PromptResponses 1}} && git checkout FETCH_HEAD"
    context: 'remotes'
    prompts:
      - type: 'input'
        title: 'Fork:'
        initialValue: "{{index .SelectedRemote.Name }}"
      - type: 'input'
        title: 'Remote branch on fork:'
```
Which actually fetches some branch from a remote and then checks out the head of that branch (Useful in evaluating PRs
before merging outside Github world).
I was wondering if I can (instead of using input prompts) generate a menu prompt where options are populated
by running a command (say `git branches` for example) instead of explicitly listing them in the config section.

I'm looking for something like this:
```
  - key : 'r'
    description: 'Checkout a remote ref as FETCH_HEAD'
    command: "git fetch {{index .PromptResponses 0}} {{index .PromptResponses 1}} && git checkout FETCH_HEAD"
    context: 'remotes'
    prompts:
      - type: 'input'
        title: 'Fork:'
        initialValue: "{{index .SelectedRemote.Name }}"
      - type: 'menu'
        title: 'Remote branch on fork:'
        optionsFromCommand: 'git branch  -r --list {{index .PromptResponses 0}}/*'
```

[Line 112 from custom_commands.go](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/06a8eb115c100816e3ceccff875010a84416beee/pkg/gui/custom_commands.go#L112) kind of says i can't do this unless I add a new case in there.

So, how to capture the output of `gui.OSCommand.PrepareShellSubProcess(cmdStr)` as a string?

discard all changes

cancel

title: Confirmation box for force-deletion of branch is not displayed if system locale is not English
body:
**Describe the bug**

git [localises the error message](https://github.com/git/git/commit/49df4b0298ea87ec737221c35ac74f8e6ee108c9#diff-b8ed76af187b5cdf2a005fd57cba9f2d8704f5ed5f1e569047adbbb739367662R203-R205) which is shown when `git branch -d ${BRANCH_NAME}` is attempted on a branch which is not fully merged.

lazygit, on the other side, seems to check only the English version as a heuristic to decide when the deletion confirmation box should be shown in-UI:

https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/a2ee52142c2fe28b10d8ff5985dfd7d973a25a83/pkg/gui/branches_panel.go#L301-L303

That will not work on locales which have the git error message translated.

I think what *may* be a better heuristic is to match on whether `git branch -D` is listed in the error message. I'd like to think that all localisations should preserve that hint as to what the "make this work" command is in this context (it does at least for Polish).

I can circumvent this by always running `LC_ALL=en-US lazygit`, but it would be nice to have this work out-of-the-box.

I would even be willing to PR and test this, just wanted to make sure this is indeed desired as per the contribution guidelines.

**To Reproduce**

Bit tricky because locales are involved, but it can be done.

1. Create a branch which diverges off the main branch and has unmerged commits
2. Run `LC_ALL=pl-PL lazygit`, for instance (but any other locale that has a translated variant works in order to reproduce)
3. Attempt to delete branch created in step (1)

**Expected behavior**

lazygit should show the confirmation box it shows in English:

![2021-08-14-135236_1126x71_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/129445437-d4e67113-7799-430c-a272-2677f6f22c6a.png)

A generic "error occurred" message is shown instead:

probably hours if I leave it be). This seems to be happening virtually every time my laptop wakes up from sleeping
(suspend to ram I think is the correct term). Just now, as an example, I opened my laptop, checked htop for heavy CPU
users, and lazygit was floating around 23-26%. I had multiple instance (on different repos) opened at the same time.
After closing all of them, and restarting a single instance, CPU usage is 0 again, as I would expect given that the app
is not doing anything. Opening multiple instances back again does not seem to bring the CPU usage up either, even after
waiting for a few minutes (doing nothing, just leaving the app open).


**To Reproduce**

title: Better keybinding support
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Tcell has support for a wide range of key combinations (e.g. ctrl+right-arrow) but our gocui package (which plugs into tcell) doesn't handle them properly. In `vendor/github.com/jesseduffield/gocui/tcell_driver.go` we currently set the modifier to 0 (ModNone) if it's set to Ctrl or Shift.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We need to do the following:
1) don't swallow tcell modifiers in `vendor/github.com/jesseduffield/gocui/tcell_driver.go`
2) In `pkg/gui/keybindings.go`, instead of doing this:
```go
		{
			ViewName:    "files",
			Contexts:    []string{string(FILES_CONTEXT_KEY)},
			Key:         gui.getKey("<c-right>"),
			Handler:     gui.myHandler,
			Description: gui.Tr.MyDescription,
			Modifier:    gocui.ModNone,
		},
```
We should either have our `getKey` function also return a modifier, or have a separate `gui.getModifier("<c-right>")` call which gives us the correct modifier from the key.

Because I was too lazy to do this in the past, I introduced a bit of tech debt by having tcell's `tcell.KeyF64` map to our `gocui.KeyAltEnter`. We should instead just have that as `gocui.KeyEnter` with the `ModAlt` modifier.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
none

**Additional context**
* related PR that attempted to work on this problem when we were using termbox instead of tcell: https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/pull/1142
* Addressing this issue will require changes both in this repo and in https://github.com/jesseduffield/gocui (but because we use a vendor directory you can make the changes locally there while you're hacking away)
* For some reason, tcell itself has some keys that seem to encode the fact that Ctrl is being held (see for example `KeyCtrlE` in `vendor/github.com/gdamore/tcell/v2/key.go`. I'm not sure why that's the case if tcell makes use of a ctrl modifier

title: Fuzzy find files for showing file history
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Sometimes I want to show all commits for a given file to see all changes for that single file. `lazygit` already has this feature when you press `<ctrl-s>` (_"view filter-by-path options..."_) but you have to enter the path by hand without the ability to search or autocomplete the path.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

At the moment my workflow looks like this:

- I'm hitting `<ctrl-s>` (_"enter path to filter by"_)
- then I'm hitting `:` (_"execute custom command"_)
- then I'm entering / opening [nnn](https://github.com/jarun/nnn) with `nnn -x`
- I'm searching the file that I'm looking for and copy the path
- I'm leaving `nnn` and hit `<cmd+v>` to paste the copied path into the dialog that `lazygit` is still showing

So in general everything is working as expected but it's a little bit cumbersome and not so convenient / intuitive.

**Additional context**

See also the discussion here https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/discussions/1377

title: Feature Request: commit message length warning
body:
There's a convention that the line length of commit messages [should be limited to 50/72 characters](https://stackoverflow.com/a/11993051/13213436).

Both VSCode ([git.inputValidationLength](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_28#_configure-long-commit-message-warning-threshold)) and Vim ([gitcommitSummary](https://github.com/tpope/vim-git/blob/master/syntax/gitcommit.vim#L22)) have features where the editor will warn you when the length of the current line of the commit message is greater than a configured limit.

It would be nice if lazygit had this same functionality where a warning will be displayed in the commit message input prompt if the current line length is greater than the configuration setting `commitLengthWarning: <int>`.

If I switch branches from the command line while lazygit is open, then return to lazygit and reword a commit, lazygit doesn't realize that I've switched branches. The commit gets reworded OK, but the end result is that the new branch gets hard-reset to point to the reworded commit (which was from the other branch). The commits that were on the other branch are orphaned. So to get them back generally requires looking in the reflog.

**To Reproduce**

Open lazygit in one terminal while we're on a branch (in this case, "main").

In a separate terminal, confirm the state of our two branches - "main" and "side-project", then switch to the "side-project" branch:

```
>>> git log main 
commit 3ad567a960729a963a4ac6ae6098cd51baba2b0b (HEAD -> main)
    Added c.txt

commit 6c69d3e272aa90be402c1c21f4f60031dccab300
    Added a

>>> git log side-project 
commit 460481cf893ef501d3da847e277d7da257471db4 (side-project)
    Added b.txt

commit 6c69d3e272aa90be402c1c21f4f60031dccab300
    Added a

>>> git co side-project 
Switched to branch 'side-project'
```

Back in lazygit, switch to the commits panel (4) then reword (R), enter a new commit description for the commit "Added c.txt" -> "Added c.txt (reworded").

Return to the separate terminal to see what happened:

```
>>> git log side-project 
commit ecee69ce24f8bc0215633cc2b2b46d4ae679b39f (HEAD -> side-project)
    Added c.txt (reworded)

commit 6c69d3e272aa90be402c1c21f4f60031dccab300
    Added a

>>> git log main 
commit 3ad567a960729a963a4ac6ae6098cd51baba2b0b (main)
    Added c.txt

commit 6c69d3e272aa90be402c1c21f4f60031dccab300
    Added a
```

Both branches now have commits that add "c.txt". The commit that adds "b.txt" is now not on either branch.

**Expected behavior**

A few possibilities come to mind:

* If lazygit thinks we're on main (when we're not) and the commit it's rewording is on main, it could reset main to point to the reworded commit.
